title: Optimized protocol for stable isotope tracing and steady-state metabolomics in mouse HER2+ breast cancer brain metastasis
protocol: Anesthetize 5–6 weeks old female athymic Nude Foxn1nu or NSG mice by injecting intraperitoneally 50 μL of Ketamine (25 mg/mL)/Xylazine (2.5 mg/mL) cocktail.
Shave hair in the chest area using a hair trimmer or remove hair using hair removal cream to identify injection point and obtain better bioluminescent images.
Place the mouse on its back with the chest facing up on a flat surface.
Stretch forelimbs and hind limbs of the anesthetized mouse and restrict any movement using paper tape.
Wipe the chest using Webcol.
Mark the injection spot targeting left ventricle on the front and middle of the chest, slightly left of the sternum between sternal notch and top of xiphoid process.
Mix cells in Eppendorf tube using 1 mL pipette before drawing cells into syringe.
Draw 100 μL of cells into 26G tuberculin syringe slip tip with intradermal bevel needle.
Create an air space between plunger and meniscus to see cardiac pulse.
Hold the syringe upright and insert needle in the marked spot.
Check for blood flow into the syringe.
Press the plunge slowly and inject cells into the heart.
Remove the needle in straight position to avoid heart puncture.
Retro-orbitally inject 100 μL of 50 mM D-luciferin.
Let the mouse recover on heat pad for 5 min.
Check distribution of cells by BLI imaging with exposure time of 30–60 s.
Measure metastatic incidence using BLI imaging every week or every two weeks.
Anesthetize animals using isoflurane in an anesthesia induction chamber.
Inject 100 μL of D-luciferin through the retro-orbital sinus.
Place mice nose into the nose cone of the imaging system platform.
Obtain a BLI image with exposure time of 30–60 seconds.
Look for signal in brain or organ of interest.
If signal is saturated, reduce exposure time.
Determine whole body average photon flux and brain only photon flux using image analysis software.
Faster mice for 12-16 hours before 13C-glucose and 13C-glutamine infusion to achieve higher fractional enrichment in plasma.
Anesthetize mice by injecting intraperitoneally 30 mg/mL of ketamine/xylazine (50 μL).
Later, anesthetize mice with 20 mg/mL of ketamine hydrochloride (50 μL).
Place a 20-gauge catheter in the lateral tail vein of each anesthetized mouse.
Infuse 13C6-glucose intravenously as a bolus of 0.6 mg/g body mass over 1 min in 150 μL of saline using a programmable multi syringe holding pump system.
Next, infuse a bolus of 0.0138 mg/g body mass per minute for 3–4 h (in a volume of 150–200 μL/h) using the same procedure.
Infuse 13C5-glutamine as a bolus of 0.2125 mg/g body mass over 1 min in 150 μL of saline.
Next, infuse a bolus of 0.004 mg/g body mass per minute for 5–6 h (in a volume of 150–200 μL/h) using a programmable multi syringe holding pump system.
Monitor mice continuously throughout the infusion experiment (3 h for glucose infusion, and 5 h for glutamine infusion).
Collect blood every hour by retro-orbital puncture into an EDTA tube.
Keep tubes on ice after labeling.
If mice appear weak, collect blood once every two hours.
Inject 100 μL of D-luciferin through the retro-orbital sinus post-infusion.
Obtain bioluminescent images to locate brain metastatic lesions.
Perform intracardial perfusion using 15–20 mL of 1× PBS in a syringe connected to a 23G butterfly needle.
Isolate the brain by removing the skull carefully after perfusion.
Obtain ex vivo brain bioluminescent images using an IVIS machine.
Identify metastatic lesions using BLI signal.
Resect BLI+ brain metastatic lesion using surgical blades.
Verify BLI signal in the resected metastatic lesion using an IVIS imager.
Minimize number of non-tumor cells in the collected tissue by precisely cutting only regions with high BLI signal.
Flash freeze collected tissues in liquid nitrogen and store at −80°C.
Homogenize 30–50 mg of metastatic lesion using an electronic tissue disruptor (Qiagen) in 1 mL chilled 80% methanol (LC-MS grade, Fisher Scientific).
Subject the homogenized solution to three freeze-thaw cycles using liquid nitrogen and 37°C water bath.
Centrifuge samples at 13,000 g for 10 min to precipitate macromolecules.
Collect supernatant carefully and lyophilize using Speed-Vac.
Process blood samples for metabolite analysis within one hour.
Store blood samples on ice and centrifuge at 2,500 g at 4°C for 10 min.
Collect blood plasma (top yellow layer) carefully and freeze at −80°C.
Add 10–15 μL of blood plasma to 80:20 methanol: water.
Subject the mixture to evaporation using Speed-Vac.
Isolate the brain from mice once the average photon flux reached 106–107 p/sec/cm2/sr after D-luciferin injection and cardiac perfusion.
Mark metastatic lesions using ex vivo brain BLI signal.
Surgically remove metastatic lesions, selecting regions with high BLI signals to minimize non-tumor cells.
Use BLI negative regions as controls for normalization from the same region in mice without brain metastasis.
Flash freeze tumors in liquid nitrogen and store at −80°C until further processing.
Homogenize metastatic lesions (30–50 mg) using an electronic tissue disruptor in 1 mL chilled 80% methanol.
Follow three freeze-thaw cycles by using liquid nitrogen and a 37°C water bath.
Centrifuge samples at 13,000 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Collect supernatant and lyophilize using a Speed-Vac.
Resuspend lyophilized samples with 40–60 μL of anhydrous pyridine containing methoxyamine.
Vortex the solution and transfer it to a GC-MS autoinjector vial.
Heat the vial at 70°C for 10 minutes.
Add 80–120 μL N-(tert-butyldimethylsilyl)-N-methyltrifluoroacetamide (MTBSTFA) derivatization reagent to each vial.
Vortex to mix and heat the vials at 70°C for 1 hour.
Inject 1 μL of sample into Agilent 7890 gas chromatograph coupled with mass selective detector Agilent 5975C.
Process the obtained raw data using maven software with an in-house optimized database.
Export files as spreadsheet (.csv).
Resuspend lyophilized samples for steady state metabolite analysis in 100 μL of 0.1% formic acid in water.
Transfer the solution to vials with pre-slit screw caps.
Perform data acquisition using reverse-phase chromatography on a 1290 UHPLC liquid chromatography (LC) system.
Interface the LC system to a high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) 6550 iFunnel Q-TOF mass spectrometer.
Operate MS in both positive and negative modes (ESI+ and ESI-).
Separate analytes using an Acquity UPLC® HSS T3 column.
Keep the column at 20°C–22°C.
Mix mobile phase A with 0.1% formic acid in water.
Mix mobile phase B with 0.1% formic acid in 100% acetonitrile (ACN).
Set flow rate to 250 μL/min.
Inject 5 μL of sample for analysis.
Set dry gas temperature to 225°C and flow to 18 L/minute.
Set fragmentor voltage to 175 V.
Set sheath gas temperature to 350°C and flow to 12 L/min.
Set nozzle voltage to 500 V.
Set capillary voltage to +3,500 V in positive mode and −3,500 V in negative mode.
Acquire data over the full m/z range of 40–1,700 in both modes at a rate of 1 spectrum per second in profile format.

Process raw data files using Profinder B.08.00 SP3 software with an in-house database created under same analysis conditions and determined retention time and accurate mass information on 600 standards.
Set mass tolerance to 10 ppm for matching parameters.
Set retention time tolerance to 0.5 min for matching parameters.
Manually curate peak integration results in Profinder for improved consistency.
Export curated data as a spreadsheet (.csv).
Normalize obtained data to natural abundance of the isotope 13C (1.109%).
Normalize obtained data to infused isotopes, such as glucose or glutamine in blood plasma.
